notes:
This typescript is headed “Résumé de quelques résultats de Kostant (sous groupes simples de rang 1).” Its handwritten reference gives “The principal 3-dimensional subgroup...., Am. Jour. Oct.1959” and section numbers 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 1.2, 9.3. “Oct.1959” belongs to the citation, not to a composition date. The archive sheet number is 15. No total page count is written here. No source “à vérifier”, “sauf erreur”, “je présume” or explicit mathematical question mark occurs on the page; cancellations and our reading doubts must not be presented as the author’s mathematical reservations.

Theorem 1(i) compares weight-space conditions on x,e with a homomorphism from Sl(2,k), then asserts semisimplicity/integration of x and uniqueness for the prescribed pair. Part (ii) states existence for nilpotent e, its exponential formulation, and conjugacy under a centralizer; the last sentence continues onto the following selected scan. These general existence, integration and conjugacy assertions are carried as background here, not proved by the transcription. The empty slot in “le sous-espace propre de [blank]” is left empty; neither ad(x) nor x is supplied.

Mathematics prompted separate ink checks at b), d), and “lorsque e=0 i.e. u≠1”. The visible target in b) is g(-2), and the equality e=0 is not crossed. An explicit integer 2-by-2 certificate, `math_checks/123_016_sl2_certificate.json`, uses e=E12, h=diag(1,-1), f=E21 and obtains [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=-2f, [e,f]=h, [e,h]=-2e and ad(e)^2(f)=-2e. For this example d) holds and a) holds (the odd weight spaces are zero; weight ±2 are one-dimensional; higher weights are zero), while ad(e) does not map g(0) to g(-2). The literal b) target is therefore incompatible with this standard example. More generally Jacobi gives [x,[e,v]]=[[x,e],v]+[e,[x,v]]=(k+2)[e,v] for v of weight k: ad(e) raises weight by two. This identifies the sign problem without changing it in the text.

The same certificate gives e²=0, exp(e)=I+e, log(I+e)=e and exp(0)=I. Thus the printed implication “e=0 i.e. u≠1” is false as written; e=0 corresponds to u=1. A separate slash stands beside the first point of i.e., not across the equality. Its intended target cannot be recovered and is not silently moved. The second f in d) retains a double/single-prime doubt: the expectation of a first differential does not settle two visible strokes.

A conditional check of the canceled b′) is useful but does not explain why it was canceled: if its final word is bijectif and its target is g(2), surjectivity need not imply bijectivity. In Sl(2)×Sl(2), with x=(h,0), e=(e,0), the first factor maps onto the weight-2 line while the entire second Lie algebra lies in the weight-0 kernel. This is recorded as a check of a conditional reading, not a proof of its wording.

The centralizer equality was checked conditionally in a faithful matrix realization: a matrix commuting with e commutes with the finite polynomial exp(e), and conversely one commuting with u=exp(e) commutes with the finite polynomial log(u)=e. This proves the equality for nilpotent/unipotent matrices in characteristic zero; existence of a suitable faithful realization is carried as background. The small diagonal marks above e in the first Cent(e) are preserved rather than used to create a new mathematical variable.

For the Lie-algebra uniqueness clause with fixed x,e, an actual targeted argument is available. In the finite-dimensional adjoint Sl2-module, a difference v between two possible images of the lowering generator has H-weight -2 and Ev=0. If v≠0, choose the first m≥1 with F^m v=0; such m exists because the nonzero vectors F^j v would have distinct weights. The identity E F^m v=m(λ-m+1)F^(m-1)v, for λ=-2, has nonzero coefficient -m(m+1), a contradiction in characteristic zero. Hence v=0. This checks uniqueness of the Lie-algebra triple only; the group homomorphism/integration conclusion is not claimed from this argument alone.

Pre-freeze notation review: the first L of Lie(i)(1) has two distinct offset stems and is transcribed with mathbb under the stipulated double-strike convention. The initial TikZ overlay was revised to the required alphabet representation; ordinary later Lie occurrences are unchanged.


Cross-page notation review: existing crops on this leaf resolve the typed round indices as lowercase o by their x-height. The handwritten rings in b) and the (ii) addition remain o/0 doubtful, as do the handwritten Z indices on 123/017. This clarifies the scope of the uncertainty without changing the already transcribed first-candidate o letters.
